references.text: You shall bring the firstfruits of your land's harvest to the house of the Lord your God. Both verses speak about giving the firstfruits as an offering to the Lord.
Refers to the wave offering (תְרוּמָה) that the Israelites were to give to the Lord, the same type of offering mentioned in Numbers 15:20.
Concerns bringing the firstfruits of the harvest as a wave offering before the Lord, parallel to the command to give the firstfruits of the dough.
Mentions the firstfruits of grain that are to be given to the priests, corresponding to the firstfruits of the dough in Numbers 15:20.
Describes the command to take the firstfruits of all the fruit of the land and bring them to the chosen place of the Lord, the same principle as the firstfruits of the dough.
The Israelites committed themselves to bringing the firstfruits of their dough to the priests, a direct fulfillment of the command in Numbers 15:20.
The prophet Ezekiel repeats the command that the firstfruits of every kind of firstfruit and all wave offerings shall belong to the priests, including the firstfruits of the dough.
Encourages honoring the Lord with the firstfruits of all harvests, the same principle of giving the first and best to God.
Paul uses the image of the firstfruits of the dough (ἀπαρχὴ τοῦ φυράματος) as holy, with direct reference to this command to explain Israel's holiness.
